title: LIFL: A Lightweight, Event-driven Serverless Platform for Federated Learning
problem: Federated learning systems require stateful coordination of distributed participants across network communication, which conflicts with the stateless, short-lived execution model of serverless platforms. Deploying FL on serverless infrastructure incurs high orchestration overhead and coordination latency.
motivation: Serverless platforms offer elastic, cost-effective compute, but FL systems need efficient, low-overhead orchestration; combining them enables privacy-preserving distributed training at scale without infrastructure burden.
method: LIFL models FL orchestration as event-driven workflows where serverless functions handle participant registration, parameter aggregation, and model updates triggered by completion events rather than polling or persistent connections. Lightweight event handlers coordinate training rounds asynchronously, reducing long-running stateful processes and leveraging serverless platform elasticity.
key_novelty: Event-driven serverless architecture that decouples FL orchestration from stateful coordination, eliminating overhead of traditional centralized parameter servers.
contributions: Event-driven orchestration model for federated learning on serverless
Lightweight platform design eliminating coordinator overhead
Asynchronous parameter aggregation via event triggers
Integration with serverless infrastructure (AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions)
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in title alone; likely involves maximum participant scale or communication overhead inherent to event-driven models.
primary_theme: Event-driven serverless platform for federated learning
